mechanisms.name: privateKey.rotationPolicy default flips to Always: mesh-root-ca (cert-manager namespace) root CA key rotation on renewal
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: Yes, this change affects this environment, and the upgrade is not safe as-is.
resourcesConsumers: mesh-root-ca Certificate (cert-manager namespace), self-signed root signed by selfsigned-bootstrap
mesh-ca ClusterIssuer (signs every leaf with mesh-root-ca)
mechanisms.mechanism: No Certificate sets rotationPolicy, so mesh-root-ca inherits the new default Always. On 1.17 renewal reused the key, so existing leaf chains and every ca.crt copy stayed valid. On 1.18 the renewal (about 11 months after issue in prod: duration 8760h, renewBefore 720h) creates a new key pair, which is a different trust anchor. mesh-ca then signs with the new key, but cert-manager does not re-issue leaves when the issuer's CA changes. ledger-tls and checkout-tls renew on their own schedules (renewBefore 240h on a 720h duration, about every 20 days at different offsets), and each service takes its trust anchor from its own Secret's ca.crt. Until both have renewed, the two sides can disagree on the root: ledger rejects checkout's old-CA client cert, or checkout's curl fails to verify ledger's old-CA server cert. The window can last up to about 20 days. Symptom: checkout logs "ledger call failed" and payments mTLS fails. Nothing breaks at upgrade time; it only takes effect at the next re-issue.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Preferred: before bumping the pin, set privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never explicitly on mesh-root-ca (in the base manifests) to keep same-key renewal. Adding an explicit rotationPolicy: Never does not change the key and should not cause a re-issue. Stopgap: set config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false in platform/cert-manager/values.yaml, which only defers the problem because 1.19 removes the gate. If the root key should be rotated at some point, plan it as a deliberate migration with a trust overlap (distribute both old and new CA to the consumers before switching)

mechanisms.name: privateKey.rotationPolicy default flips to Always: ledger-tls and checkout-tls leaf key rotation
resourcesConsumers: checkout (re-reads its cert and key on every curl)
ledger (nginx loads tls.crt and tls.key at startup)
mechanisms.mechanism: Each renewal now produces a new ECDSA P-256 key. That is the intended security behaviour and works with mTLS as long as the CA stays the same. checkout follows a renewal immediately. ledger's nginx does not reload tls.crt/tls.key when the files change, so it keeps serving the old, still-valid pair until it restarts or reloads. This is already true today, but with key rotation the files now contain a new key, so a restart or reload is what picks up the new pair. The repo has no reloader or checksum annotation that would trigger one.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Rotation works with mTLS as long as the CA stays the same. No key pinning or other consumer of the leaf public keys was found in the repo. For the leaves, either set Never too or accept Always, which is the secure default.
citedEvidence: nginx (ledger) loads tls.crt and tls.key at startup and does not reload them on file change
checkout re-reads its cert and key files on every curl
No reloader or checksum annotation in the repo
No key pinning or other consumer of the leaf public keys found in the repo

recommendedValidation: Leaf test: renew ledger-tls alone and confirm what nginx serves before and after a restart

overall.recommendation: Do not proceed as-is. Before bumping the pin, either set privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never explicitly on mesh-root-ca (preferred), or set config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false as a stopgap until 1.19, which removes the gate.
